{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABgNK5lw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhJqKoE", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 162, "title": "Simplify Help, expose display controls and GitHub link, and remove About/Legal UI", "body": "## Problem

The browser emulator currently puts important display settings behind a long **Help / Controls** disclosure, while a separate **About / Legal** disclosure adds substantial text to the first-level navigation. The header does not provide a visible link to the actual GitHub repository. The result is unnecessarily text-heavy and hides simple, frequently useful choices.

On current `main` (`5f11dab5f1e11216e70a6eeab07bd3ec43480d14`), [`web/index.html`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/index.html) shows two header disclosures. Help includes the complete keyboard mapping, gamepad/touch guidance, audio notes, **Scale**, **Display**, ROM privacy, SRAM persistence and recovery explanations. About/Legal contains the product introduction, game rights/provenance text and the game notice link. The app already uses a concise, emulator-first layout and complete portrait/landscape controller UI.

The maintainer wants a cleaner first view, with **Scale**, **Display** and the **GitHub project link visible directly** and a **much smaller Help**. The **About / Legal UI should be removed**, not replaced with another big disclosure or a long prose block.

## Expected outcome

- **Remove the About / Legal disclosure from the browser UI** entirely. Its redundant product description does not need to appear elsewhere on the page.
- **Simplify Help / Controls** into a small, quickly scannable reference for how to operate the emulator (e.g., concise keyboard mapping and essential touch/gamepad hints). Move nonessential lengthy explanations to existing README/documentation, rather than replacing the old long paragraphs with new ones. Help should be optional reference material, not required onboarding.
- Move the existing **Scale** and **Display (CRT / Pixel)** selectors **out of Help**, making them continuously visible, compact and directly discoverable in the main interface. Choose a deliberate layout: near the screen or in a slim group of display controls, not mixed into cartridge selection or the playback/volume semantics. Preserve current scale values, persisted CRT/Pixel preference, default CRT, WebGL fallback, and live switching.
- Add a clearly recognizable, always-visible **GitHub** link to `https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust`, preferably in the header, on desktop and both mobile orientations. Use a short text label and/or recognizable icon with accessible name; avoid a large promotional button.
- Keep **snes-rust / the emulator screen** as the visual focus. Minimize explanatory copy; use alignment, spacing and group boundaries to communicate what belongs together. Follow the [README UI/UX principles](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/README.md#uiux): **Keep it simple; Show, don't tell; Intuitive and predictable**.

## Legal, privacy and failure guidance (do not silently lose necessary information)

The maintainer's request is to remove the prominent **About / Legal panel**, not to change game ownership, ROM distribution permission or licensing. Keep the authoritative [`demos/NOTICE.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/demos/NOTICE.md), [README](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust#readme), and MIT-vs-ROM rights distinction intact; check that visitors can reasonably reach ROM provenance/permissions through the visible GitHub link and README/NOTICE links. If a compact direct 'Notices' link is actually needed for discoverability/compliance, place it unobtrusively (not another About/Legal disclosure or repeated game-rights prose). Do not assert that the game ROMs are MIT-licensed or freely redistributable.

Keep current local-ROM privacy guarantees and the on-screen **actionable** save failure/restore, blocked sound, and graphics fallback messages. Background explanatory details can live in README/Help, but never conceal a recovery action or remove a necessary warning. Preserve current CSP and safe external-link behavior.

## Scope and implementation notes

- Prefer limited, semantic changes in `web/index.html`, `web/style.css`, any needed JS selectors, browser tests and concise README/help references. No new framework, router, settings system, extra ROM, shader implementation or core change.
- The two selectors must remain keyboard, touch and screen-reader accessible, with correct labels, focus states and actual values. Moving them must not break `#scale`/`#display` event listeners, display preference persistence or the WebGL-to-Pixel fallback.
- Desktop should retain a large, readable game screen. On narrow **portrait**, avoid a tall row of header widgets that pushes the 12 SNES controls below the viewport. On short-height **landscape**, retain the center screen, left D-pad and right face/shoulder clusters without clipping/overlays or crowding with header controls; make Scale and Display visible but compact and usable.
- Link to the repository using real navigation (new tab optional with `rel="noopener noreferrer"` if appropriate). The URL must work on GitHub Pages subpaths; no requirement for new third-party assets, tracking scripts or special icons.
- The cartridge slot/Insert cartridge action, the two bundled demos, local ROM flow, one Play/Pause, Reset-to-playing, volume/mute, gamepad/keyboard and 12-button multitouch remain unchanged. Do not add extra instructions or a new About/Settings modal just to reorganize content.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Actual UI has **no About / Legal disclosure**, no long promotional/legal paragraphs in the top-level page, and a concise useful Help/Controls reference. The rights/provenance notice remains intact and readily accessible via the linked repository/README or a modest direct notice link.
- [ ] **Scale and Display are visible without opening Help**, on initial load and while a game is playing, with current values and working keyboard/touch interaction. Scale renders as before; CRT remains the default for a fresh user and explicit Pixel/CRT selections persist. GPU failure fallback still updates the selected state and message.
- [ ] A visible **GitHub** link goes to `https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust` and is accessible via keyboard and mobile touch.
- [ ] Demonstrate the grouping/hierarchy with actual implementation screenshots at desktop 1280×900, narrow portrait ~320×740 and short landscape ~667×320 or smaller. Game screen stays the visual focus, touch controls remain operable, no horizontal overflow or significant lost screen space.
- [ ] Update production-browser DOM/interaction tests for the new layout and removed disclosure. Check link destination, selector visibility/function, focus/keyboard navigation, layout, help readability, legal-notice reachability and output/error messaging; preserve existing real Wasm game tests and responsive touch tests.
- [ ] Run and report the applicable production build, full browser/Pages tests and relevant CI checks. Do not weaken tests merely to accommodate markup changes; report unrun checks accurately.
- [ ] Document the small before/after UX rationale and avoid needless new CSS/JS abstractions or compatibility scaffolding for a removed About/Legal panel.

## Optional validation

Physical iOS Safari/Android Chrome and screen-reader usability inspection.

## Required post-merge verification

Once merged, inspect the new `main` GitHub Pages workflow and the actual published site in desktop/portrait/landscape viewports, including the visible GitHub link and both live Scale/Display selectors. Record the run and results; post-merge-only, not a pre-merge gate. On failure, create a linked `task` issue with evidence when invoked—no implied background monitoring.

- [#116](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/116): responsive touch controller layout.
- [#142](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/142): CRT/Pixel display selector.
- [#147](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/147): CRT default.
